letter-a.context: A plain capital A drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. Teachers and quiz apps use it for grade A and answer A.

letter-b.context: The capital letter B, the second letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. It also labels plan B, grade B and answer B.

letter-c.context: Capital C on its own, set to match the icon stroke, for letter labels, sorting by name and reading apps for kids. It also marks grade C, answer C and the Roman numeral for 100.

letter-d.context: A plain capital D drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. It also marks grade D, answer D and the Roman numeral for 500.

letter-e.context: The capital letter E, the fifth letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. On a compass or map it stands for east.

letter-f.context: Capital F on its own, set to match the icon stroke, for letter labels, sorting by name and reading apps for kids. In grading it marks a fail, and in lists it labels option F.

letter-g.context: A plain capital G drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. As a unit it is the symbol for grams.

letter-h.context: The capital letter H, the eighth letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. On signs it marks helipads and hospitals.

letter-i.context: Capital I on its own, set to match the icon stroke, for letter labels, sorting by name and reading apps for kids. It is also the Roman numeral for one.

letter-j.context: A plain capital J drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. In physics it is the symbol for the joule, and on playing cards it marks the jack.

letter-k.context: The capital letter K, the eleventh letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. It is shorthand for thousand, as in 10k, and marks the king on playing cards.

letter-l.context: Capital L on its own, set to match the icon stroke, for letter labels, sorting by name and reading apps for kids. On clothing tags it means large, and in Roman numerals it is 50.

letter-m.context: A plain capital M drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. On clothing tags it means medium, it abbreviates million, and in Roman numerals it is 1000.

letter-n.context: The capital letter N, the fourteenth letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. On a compass or map it stands for north.

letter-o.context: Capital O on its own, set to match the icon stroke, for letter labels, sorting by name and reading apps for kids. In chemistry it is the symbol for oxygen.

letter-p.context: A plain capital P drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. On road signs and maps it marks parking.

letter-q.context: The capital letter Q, the seventeenth letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. It shows up in Q and A sections and marks the queen on playing cards.

letter-r.context: Capital R on its own, set to match the icon stroke, for letter labels, sorting by name and reading apps for kids. It also labels rows and option R in lettered lists.

letter-s.context: A plain capital S drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. On clothing tags it means small, and on a compass it stands for south.

letter-t.context: The capital letter T, the twentieth letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. Design apps often use a T for the text or type tool.

letter-u.context: Capital U on its own, set to match the icon stroke, for letter labels, sorting by name and reading apps for kids. It also labels option U in lettered lists and unit fields.

letter-v.context: A plain capital V drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. It is the Roman numeral for five and a short form of version and volt.

letter-w.context: The capital letter W, the twenty-third letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. On a compass it stands for west, and as a unit it is the watt.

letter-x.context: Capital X on its own, set to match the icon stroke, for letter labels, sorting by name and reading apps for kids. It is the Roman numeral for ten and the usual name for an unknown in algebra.

letter-y.context: A plain capital Y drawn in a single stroke weight, used for initials, monograms, alphabet lessons and labels. In algebra and charts it names the y variable and the vertical axis.

letter-z.context: The capital letter Z, the twenty-sixth letter of the Latin alphabet, for avatars without a photo, spelling apps and lettered labels. As the last letter it closes A to Z lists, and in 3D it names the depth axis.

number-0.context: The digit 0 (zero) drawn as a single line figure, for counts, keypads, scores and numbered labels. It shows empty counters, zero balances and the 0 key on keypads.

number-1.context: A plain numeral 1, the number one, for counters, number pads, ratings and math lessons for kids. It marks first place, step one and single items.
